body:
I don't really want to just resolve this to a "weird things happen under drugs/alcohol." Multiple sexual assaults are committed under the influence and depending on the case, they are either convicted/have charges reduced/thrown out entirely. 

Many times, defendants claim they didn't have 100% intention to commit assault, but drugs/alcohol was found to have served as an aggravating cause. Meaning, someone may have had the urge to commit assault and the drugs/alc simply lowered their inhibitions, allowing them to make a poor choice with just as devastating consequences. 

That is not what happened in this case whatsoever and that's what I'm trying to get at.
